files.lesson.md: --- order: 13 unit: fractions node: AC9M7N06 n2 uses: [AC9M7N04 n1] # simplifying fractions (Equivalent fractions) title: Multiplying and dividing fractions summary: "a/b × c/d is c/d of a/b: multiply the tops and multiply the bottoms. Multiplying by a fraction less than 1 makes a number smaller. Dividing asks how many fit: 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12." language: maths connection: bottle-fill # data/connections/maths.yml voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Three quarters of a pizza is left, and you eat half of what is left. How much of the whole pizza did you eat? Fractions of fractions are multiplications." app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8270 url: http://127.0.0.1:8270/index.html readySelector: "#sl-c" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: area.yml#explain-pic, caption: "$\\tfrac{3}{4}$ of $\\tfrac{2}{3}$: the purple overlap is 6 of the 12 small parts, so $\\tfrac{2}{3} \\times \\tfrac{3}{4} = \\tfrac{6}{12} = \\tfrac{1}{2}$." } explainClip: query: { code: "@area.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "A fraction of a fraction" say: "Multiplying fractions takes a fraction of a fraction." clip: - caption: { text: "2/3 of the square is blue.", say: "Two thirds of the square is blue." } - wait: 800 - caption: { text: "Take 3/4 of it: 3 of 4 rows.", say: "Now take three quarters of it." } - click: Make c bigger - click: Make c bigger - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "6/12" } - wait: 600 - caption: { text: "6 of 12 parts: tops × tops, bottoms × bottoms.", say: "Six of twelve parts: multiply the tops and the bottoms." } - wait: 1400 --- "Of" means multiply: $\tfrac{1}{3}$ of 12 is $\tfrac{1}{3} \times 12 = 4$. A fraction of a fraction works the same way: $\tfrac{3}{4}$ of $\tfrac{2}{3}$ is $\tfrac{2}{3} \times \tfrac{3}{4}$. ## Predict: half of a third ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to whether 1/2 × 1/3 is bigger or smaller than 1/2 surfaces the belief that multiplying always makes bigger." check: type: predict q: "Is $\\tfrac{1}{2} \\times \\tfrac{1}{3}$ bigger or smaller than $\\tfrac{1}{2}$?" options: ["Smaller", "Bigger", "The same"] actual: "Smaller: 1/2 × 1/3 = 1/6, a third of a half. Multiplying by a number less than 1 takes only part." ``` Think of it as $\tfrac{1}{3}$ of $\tfrac{1}{2}$. ## Run: a third of a half ```step stage: run insight: "Shading 1/2 of the columns and 1/3 of the rows shows the overlap is 1/6: smaller than both." try: { playground: board, starter: "area.yml#run", height: 620 } check: { type: board, text: "The board shows $\\tfrac{1}{2}$ of the square. Change $c$ and $d$ to show $\\tfrac{1}{2} \\times \\tfrac{1}{3}$. Was your prediction right?", when: "a = 1 and b = 2 and c = 1 and d = 3", explain: "The overlap is 1 of 6 parts: 1/2 × 1/3 = 1/6." } ``` $a$ of $b$ columns are blue; $c$ of $d$ rows are orange. The overlap is purple. To multiply fractions, **multiply the tops and multiply the bottoms**: no common denominator needed. The square shows why: the parts multiply, and so do the shaded ones. ## Investigate: multiply, and divide ```step stage: investigate insight: "Tops times tops and bottoms times bottoms; Jack's belief that multiplying makes bigger fails for fractions less than 1. Dividing counts how many fit, so dividing by a fraction less than 1 makes bigger." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Work out $\\tfrac{2}{3} \\times \\tfrac{3}{5}$ in simplest form." answer: "2/5" form: simplest feedback: - ["6/15", "Right amount: now simplify. 6 and 15 share 3."] - ["5/8", "That adds. To multiply, multiply the tops and the bottoms."] explain: "(2 × 3)/(3 × 5) = 6/15 = 2/5." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#jack" text: "Jack compares $\\tfrac{3}{4} \\times 20$ with 20. Click the line where his reasoning goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: multiply-makes-bigger explain: "Line 3: multiplying by a number less than 1 makes smaller. 3/4 of 20 is 15, less than 20." - check: type: answer q: "How many quarters are there in 3? Work out $3 \\div \\tfrac{1}{4}$." answer: "12" feedback: - ["3/4", "That is 3 × 1/4. Dividing asks how many quarters fit into 3."] - ["0.75", "That is 3 × 1/4. Dividing asks how many quarters fit into 3."] explain: "4 quarters in each whole, so 12 in 3: 3 ÷ 1/4 = 3 × 4 = 12." ``` ### Multiply across; divide by flipping Here is how each kind works. ```worked \tfrac{2}{3} \times \tfrac{3}{4} = \tfrac{2 \times 3}{3 \times 4} = \tfrac{6}{12} = \tfrac{1}{2} :: Multiply the tops and the bottoms, then simplify. \tfrac{3}{4} \times 20 = \tfrac{60}{4} = 15 :: A whole number is over 1: 20 = 20/1. 15 is less than 20. \tfrac{1}{2} \div 3 = \tfrac{1}{6} :: Share a half into 3: each share is a sixth (the same as × 1/3). 3 \div \tfrac{1}{4} = 3 \times 4 = 12 :: How many quarters in 3? Dividing by 1/4 is multiplying by 4. \tfrac{2}{3} \div \tfrac{1}{6} = \tfrac{2}{3} \times 6 = 4 :: Divide by a fraction: multiply by it flipped (1/6 flipped is 6/1 = 6). 0.4 \times 3 = 1.2 :: Decimals: 4 tenths × 3 = 12 tenths. ``` Now try one: $\tfrac{2}{3} \times \tfrac{3}{5}$. ### Find the mistake Read Jack's reasoning. Work out $\tfrac{3}{4}$ of 20 first. ### How many fit? ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a new product on the board, a fraction of a whole number, dividing by a whole number, dividing by a fraction, then which product is bigger than the number." try: { playground: board, starter: "area.yml#fifths", height: 620 } tasks: - starter: "area.yml#fifths" hint: "Columns: 3 of 4. Rows: 2 of 5." check: { type: board, text: "Show $\\tfrac{3}{4} \\times \\tfrac{2}{5}$ on the board.", when: "a = 3 and b = 4 and c = 2 and d = 5", explain: "6 of 20 parts: 6/20 = 3/10." } - check: type: answer q: "Work out $\\tfrac{2}{5}$ of 30." answer: "12" feedback: - ["75", "That is 30 ÷ 2/5. 'Of' means multiply: a fifth of 30 is 6."] explain: "30 ÷ 5 = 6, × 2 = 12." - check: type: answer q: "Work out $\\tfrac{3}{4} \\div 3$ in simplest form." answer: "1/4" form: simplest feedback: - ["9/4", "That is × 3. Share 3 quarters into 3 groups."] - ["3/12", "Right amount: simplify."] explain: "Share 3 quarters into 3: one quarter each. (3/4 × 1/3 = 3/12 = 1/4.)" - check: type: answer q: "Work out $\\tfrac{2}{3} \\div \\tfrac{1}{6}$." answer: "4" feedback: - ["1/9", "That multiplies. How many sixths fit in 2/3?"] - ["2/18", "That multiplies. How many sixths fit in 2/3?"] explain: "2/3 = 4/6, so four sixths fit: 2/3 × 6 = 4." - check: type: question q: "Edge case: which of these is bigger than 12?" options: ["$12 \\times \\tfrac{5}{4}$", "$12 \\times \\tfrac{3}{4}$", "$12 \\times \\tfrac{1}{2}$", "$12 \\div 2$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "3/4 is less than 1, so the answer is less than 12: 9.", "Half of 12 is 6.", "12 ÷ 2 = 6."] explain: "5/4 is more than 1, so 12 × 5/4 = 15 is bigger. Multiplying makes bigger only when the multiplier is more than 1." ``` ### Three quarters of two fifths Each task changes one thing. ### Of a whole number ### Divide by a whole number ### Divide by a fraction ### Bigger or smaller? ## Practise: multiply and divide ```step stage: practise insight: "Fractions, a decimal and a division, mixed; 'multiplying makes bigger' is the planted slip; the review keeps adding fractions fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Work out $\\tfrac{4}{5} \\times \\tfrac{5}{8}$ in simplest form." answer: "1/2" form: simplest feedback: - ["20/40", "Right amount: simplify."] explain: "20/40 = 1/2." - check: type: answer q: "A bottle holds 0.6 L. How many litres do 4 bottles hold?" answer: "2.4" feedback: - ["24", "6 tenths × 4 = 24 tenths: 2.4."] - ["0.24", "4 bottles hold more than 1 bottle: 6 tenths × 4 = 24 tenths."] explain: "0.6 × 4 = 2.4 L." - check: type: answer q: "A ribbon is $\\tfrac{3}{4}$ m long. How many pieces $\\tfrac{1}{8}$ m long can be cut from it?" answer: "6" feedback: - ["3/32", "That multiplies. How many eighths fit in 3/4?"] explain: "3/4 = 6/8: six eighths. (3/4 ÷ 1/8 = 3/4 × 8 = 6.)" smaller: check: { type: number, q: "How many pieces $\\tfrac{1}{8}$ m long fit in a whole metre?", answer: 8, explain: "Eight eighths make a whole. Now fit them into three quarters of a metre." } - check: type: answer q: "Review: work out $\\tfrac{1}{2} + \\tfrac{1}{5}$." answer: "7/10" form: simplest feedback: - ["2/7", "That adds across. Write both in tenths."] explain: "5/10 + 2/10 = 7/10." ``` ### Multiply ### Decimals ### Divide in context ### Review: adding ## Make: a quarter, another way ```step stage: make insight: "Building a product equal to 1/4 other than 1/2 × 1/2 shows many products share a value, and that simplifying is part of multiplying." try: { playground: board, starter: "area.yml#make", height: 680 } hint: ["Try 1/2 of something that is 1/2 once simplified, such as 2/4.", "Or 3/4 × 1/3."] check: { type: board, text: "Make the overlap exactly $\\tfrac{1}{4}$ of the square, without using $\\tfrac{1}{2} \\times \\tfrac{1}{2}$.", when: "v = 0.25 and q > 4 and a < b and c < d", explain: "For example 3/4 × 1/3 = 3/12, 2/4 × 1/2 = 2/8, or 2/3 × 3/8 = 6/24." } ``` Then find one where neither fraction has a 1 on top. ## Make: filling bottles, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "Dividing by a fraction asks how many fit. The paper task makes them choose to divide, expect a bigger answer, and check by multiplying back." hint: ["How many bottles of $\\tfrac{3}{4}$ L fit in 6 L?", "Dividing by a fraction less than 1 gives a bigger number."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A 6 L batch of homemade cordial goes into bottles that each hold $\\tfrac{3}{4}$ L. How many bottles can you fill?" steps: - ["I want how many $\\tfrac{3}{4}$ L fit into 6 L: $6 \\div \\tfrac{3}{4}$", "dividing counts how many fit"] - ["$6 \\div \\tfrac{3}{4} = 6 \\times \\tfrac{4}{3}$", "divide by a fraction: multiply by it flipped"] - ["$\\tfrac{24}{3} = 8$ bottles", "multiply the tops, then simplify"] - ["Check: $8 \\times \\tfrac{3}{4} = 6$ L", "8 bottles of $\\tfrac{3}{4}$ L make the whole batch"] picks: - step: 1 q: "Why is this a division?" options: - "It asks how many bottles of $\\tfrac{3}{4}$ L fit into 6 L" - "It asks for $\\tfrac{3}{4}$ of 6 L" - "It asks for 6 L more than $\\tfrac{3}{4}$ L" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "$\\tfrac{3}{4}$ of 6 L is 4.5 L, one amount, not a count of bottles.", "Nothing is being added. The question counts how many bottles fit."] answer: "8" answerLabel: "Bottles filled" feedback: - ["4.5", "That is $\\tfrac{3}{4}$ of 6. Each bottle holds less than a litre, so more than 6 bottles fit."] - ["24", "That is $6 \\times 4$. You still need to divide by the 3 on the bottom of the flipped fraction."] criteria: - "I said I was counting how many bottles fit, so I divided." - "I expected more than 6 bottles, because each holds less than 1 L." - "I checked that 8 bottles of $\\tfrac{3}{4}$ L make 6 L." explain: "6 ÷ 3/4 = 6 × 4/3 = 24/3 = 8 bottles. Check: 8 × 3/4 = 6 L. A real batch loses a little in the pot, so you might fill 7 and a bit." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The amounts are made up for the task, but a homemade drink or a school fete does face this. Say why it is a division, work it out, check by multiplying back, and type the number of bottles. **Also used in** - **Recipes.** A recipe for 4 that has to serve 30 multiplies every amount by a fraction or a whole number of the same ratio. - **Cutting.** How many $\tfrac{1}{8}$ m pieces of ribbon fit in a length is the same 'how many fit' division. - **Fuel and travel.** How many $\tfrac{3}{4}$-hour trips fit in a day uses the same division. ```teacher summary: Students use a fraction area square to see a fraction of a fraction, multiply tops and bottoms, learn that multiplying by a fraction less than 1 makes smaller, and divide by counting how many fit (AC9M7N06, node 2). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can multiply two fractions and simplify the answer. - I can divide a fraction by a whole number and by a fraction. - I can say whether a product will be bigger or smaller than the number I started with. struggle: Letting go of the belief that multiplying makes bigger. Ask for an estimate (bigger or smaller than the starting number?) before every calculation. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need equivalent fractions and simplifying, and adding fractions (previous lesson) to contrast. The one idea: a/b × c/d is c/d of a/b; the parts multiply, so the tops and the bottoms multiply. The hinge misconception is that multiplying always makes bigger (Jack's mistake); it matters for percentages next. Division is introduced as "how many fit", which justifies multiplying by the flipped fraction without a rule to memorise. running: - "Predict: students who chose bigger hold the 'multiplying makes bigger' belief. Keep the vote visible." - "Run: ask why the overlap is smaller than both shaded parts." - "Investigate: contrast with adding: no common denominator needed here." - "Modify: for the last task, ask students to sort multipliers into 'less than 1' and 'more than 1'." - "Make: collect products equal to 1/4; ask what they all simplify to." - "Paper: the bottle task is worked in books; the page marks the answer (8 bottles) and why it is a division. Books out, then look for the check 8 × 3/4 = 6." stuck: - see: A student says multiplying makes bigger (Jack's mistake). ask: What is half of 20? Is that bigger than 20? fix: "A multiplier less than 1 takes part: the answer is smaller." - see: A student finds a common denominator before multiplying. ask: Does the area picture need the same parts? fix: Multiply the tops and the bottoms; a common denominator is for adding. - see: A student multiplies when dividing by a fraction (3 ÷ 1/4 = 3/4). ask: How many quarters fit into 1? Into 3? fix: "Dividing counts how many fit: multiply by the flipped fraction." stretch: Explain with the area square why 2/3 × 3/4 = 3/4 × 2/3. support: Use the board for products; strips of paper folded into quarters for division. leads: > Next: Percentages (node 3), where taking a percentage is multiplying by a fraction of 100. Where it leads: rates and ratio, and algebraic fractions (Year 10). exit: q: Work out 3/5 × 10/12, and 2 ÷ 1/3. a: 30/60 = 1/2. 2 ÷ 1/3 = 6 (six thirds in 2). explain: > To multiply fractions, multiply the tops and multiply the bottoms, then simplify: $\tfrac{2}{3} \times \tfrac{3}{4} = \tfrac{6}{12} = \tfrac{1}{2}$. It is $\tfrac{3}{4}$ of $\tfrac{2}{3}$: in a square, 3 of 4 rows of 2 of 3 columns is 6 of 12 parts. Multiplying by a fraction less than 1 makes a number **smaller** ($\tfrac{3}{4} \times 20 = 15$). Dividing asks how many fit: $3 \div \tfrac{1}{4} = 12$, the same as $3 \times 4$. To divide by a fraction, multiply by it flipped (top and bottom swapped: $\tfrac{1}{6}$ becomes $\tfrac{6}{1} = 6$). ```

files.working.txt:
# Jack's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: jack
Which is bigger: 3/4 × 20, or 20?
3/4 × 20 means 3/4 of 20.
Multiplying always makes a number bigger.
So 3/4 × 20 is bigger than 20.
# endregion
